checks: No eclipse at 1 of 47 covered epochs where the 1.07384 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 342641246 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.0738 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.57% dimming and achieves a detection significance of 28.5 in the BLS periodogram analysis. Pixel-level image analysis yielded a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 13.5, though with a centroid offset of 18.2 arcsec from the target. Notably, no secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, an important caveat applies: the centroid determination places the dimming just 0.004 pixels closer to the target than to a nearby bright star, falling within TESS's known centroid systematic uncertainty of 0.10-0.3 pixels.
